### 2026-10-07 – # October 7: Project Research and Conceptualization!

**2h**

# October 7: Project Research and Conceptualization!

Hello! Today, I began researching PCB project ideas, aiming to find a project that had a real, impactful use, without using any advanced or time-consuming concepts. I explored ideas such as  IoT devices for smart home automation, desktop command centers for viewing time, temperature, timers, or music info, or handheld items such as PCB business cards or jewelry/watches. I weighed the pros and cons of each idea and found a few that I liked.

However, I finally decided to build a smart drink coaster! My plan is to use a temperature sensor to measure and monitor the temperature of a warm drink (probably tea or coffee) and display the temperature range the drink is in, with red, green, and blue LED's, representing hot, perfect, or cool temperature ranges, respectively.

I drew a quick sketch of the coaster to quickly visualize it:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/KvD7dTJaHVfjYIigORhVQkYxq5FrUFSP/7b30109570378adb516a64b6402308736f81565d8f414771fc5963dfd9ca34fc.png)

I also used Gemini to generate some concept art for the smart coaster, to use later when designing the frame or figuring out the layout for the inner PCB and its temperature sensor and LEDs:

![Gemini_Generated_Image_b2uofjb2uofjb2uo](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/KvD7dTJaHVfjYIigORhVQkYxq5FrUFSP/d715a8d3a53c50bb499775bff317dade899a92fa2533ecdde3fea6127473ffd9.jpg)

I also began putting together a basic components list so I can start designing the PCB layout soon:
- Microcontroller Unit (MCU)
- Contactless IR Temperature Sensor
- Status LEDs
- Enclosure/Base: 3D-printed matte grey/black housing with 3 front diffuser holes for the LEDs

As well as some optional parts for a battery power subsystem that I might or might not implement:
- LiPo Battery Charger IC
- 5V Boost Converter IC
- Lithium-Ion/LiPo Battery: 3.7V 500mAh flat LiPo cell
- Power Switch

I'm super excited to begin designing the actual PCB layout and diving deeper into this project!
